summary.text: In November 2024 remarks, Bowman said AI use must comply with current laws and regulations, including fair lending and cybersecurity, and that regulators should understand AI before considering regulatory changes; she also warned that over-regulation can prevent benefits. In August 2025, she said initial benefits of bank AI adoption were already visible and that regulatory changes ideally would occur with regulators' willing embrace. In 2026 remarks and testimony, she described AI's risks and benefits as more tangible, emphasized supporting responsible innovation while maintaining safeguards, and said the Fed with the OCC and FDIC amended model risk management guidance to clarify it does not apply to generative or agentic AI.

statements.text: Over-regulation of AI can itself present risks by preventing the realization of benefits of improved efficiency, lower operational costs, and better fraud prevention and customer service.

attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: An overly conservative regulatory approach can skew the competitive landscape by pushing activities outside of the regulated banking system or preventing the use of AI altogether.

attribution.speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Today, we are facing the rapid evolution of AI tools much earlier than many expected, and the risks and benefits are now more tangible and clear.

attribution.speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Anthropic's Mythos—an AI model that identifies cyber vulnerabilities—highlights the dynamic nature of this technology and the rapid pace that its capability can evolve.

attribution.speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Whether used in targeted modeling or enterprise-wide tools, AI will become a force multiplier for the financial system, and in the broader U.S. economy.

attribution.speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: An important part of our job as supervisors is to ensure that banks are aware of and attentive to the risks and challenges inherent in its use, so it can be deployed responsibly and effectively. And we need to ensure that there is a path for innovation, which includes the use of AI.

attribution.speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Therefore, it is necessary to ensure that our supervisory guidance does not hinder access to and implementation of innovation. This includes emphasis on the flexibility to develop, implement, and manage AI to be consistent with their unique structure, business, and culture.

attribution.speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Together with the OCC and FDIC, the Fed recently amended our model risk management guidance to clarify that it does not apply to generative or agentic AI.

attribution.speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Going forward, we expect other risk-management and governance practices to support adoption of generative and agentic AI in ways that will encourage ongoing innovation.

attribution.speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Innovation is a necessary component of financial services, and supervisory guidance should not be a barrier for banks to engage with new and evolving tools and technologies.

attribution.speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: In setting out my priorities late last year, I initiated work on a set of sound practices for financial institutions to consider in the responsible adoption and use of artificial intelligence (AI).

attribution.speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Our focus has been on supporting institutions that want to innovate responsibly by leveraging AI tools in their operations.

attribution.speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: From my perspective, financial institutions should be specific about how they use AI and whether it is material to their business operations or legal and regulatory obligations.

attribution.speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: In the report, we emphasized that lower-risk uses of AI should receive a lighter supervisory and regulatory touch.

attribution.speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: What works or is a consideration for larger institutions using AI in complex applications is not appropriate for smaller institutions with less complex AI uses.

attribution.speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: We need to ensure these practices support responsible innovation across the financial system while maintaining appropriate safeguards, especially for higher-risk applications.

attribution.speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: The financial system continues to adapt to technological advances, including the rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities and the risks and benefits of its use.

attribution.speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Recent advances in frontier AI models have dramatically accelerated the identification of cyber vulnerabilities across critical infrastructure, including the banking system.

attribution.speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: While this enhanced detection capability offers opportunities to strengthen cybersecurity defenses, it also identifies new vulnerabilities to potential cyberattacks.

attribution.speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Effectively managing these emerging cyber risks will require ongoing collaboration between public and private entities, continuous monitoring of AI developments, regular stakeholder communications, and agile regulatory and supervisory frameworks that keep pace with rapid technological change.

attribution.speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: It is important that, going forward, we ensure that there is a path to responsible innovation in the banking system, including in the use of AI.

attribution.speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Next week, the FSB's SRC will publish a report on sound practices for financial institution use of AI.

attribution.speaker: Michelle W. Bowman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: This will guide institutions in safely adopting and effectively using AI.
